classification.result: public-anchor dichotomy and P/BPP decision barrier for exact/overwhelming false-anchor annihilation

new_claims: For any explicit public linear source basis and public linear anchor, either the anchor annihilates the whole source space or an anchor-one source vector is computable by scaling one basis element.
If a deterministic polynomial-time generic compiler has anchor-one witness completeness and exact anchor annihilation on every false statement, the language is in P.
With probabilistic setup and overwhelming completeness/false-annihilation, the same public basis test puts the language in BPP.
Therefore generic exact false-anchor elimination cannot be the missing public source compiler for an NP-complete language unless the corresponding complexity collapse occurs.

Security in the non-annihilating branch cannot rely on hardness of finding anchor-one coefficients; it must rely on extra structure such as low rank/bounded factor or an independently justified computational assumption.
